post_text:
Three years ago, I rejected a pull request that added flexible, untyped JSON bags to our core settlement endpoint.

I insisted on strict, versioned schema validation with explicit field definitions instead.

The feature team pushed back hard, arguing that schema rigidity would delay client integrations by two full sprints.

I spent that weekend second-guessing myself, wondering if I was just being an obstinate purist needlessly obstructing business momentum.

Eighteen months later, an upstream partner silently changed their payload structure and decimal formats during an unannounced midnight release.

Instead of corrupting our financial ledgers with malformed records, our ingress gateway rejected the requests instantly, triggering a clean alert before any bad state persisted.

No one had to pull an all-nighter, write emergency database fix scripts, or explain missing funds to auditors.

The system held because rigid contracts quietly absorbed the human drift we could not predict.

What I learned:

Strict boundaries feel like unnecessary friction until the day undocumented changes hit your boundary.
